newsitem.title: INDIA: Kashmir journalists back boycott of government.
newsitem.headline: Kashmir journalists back boycott of government.

text.p: Journalists in troubled Kashmir on Monday voted to continue a boycott of all Indian government functions and statements unless three police officials accused of beating reporters are suspended.
At least 20 Kashmiri journalists were injured on Friday when police fired tear gas and used batons against demonstrating reporters, witnesses said.

The journalists were protesting against the alleged use of police force against reporters covering a women's demonstration earlier in the day in the summer capital of Jammu and Kashmir state, Srinagar.

"All the members of the press community shall continue their total boycott of all government functions and statements until the just and legitimate demand of suspension of three identified police officials is announced by the government," the Kashmir journalists' union said in a statement.
After the incidents last week, Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Farooq Abdullah told journalists he would order an inquiry. "But in future you also behave properly," he warned.
Kashmiri journalists have been the targets of attacks by both guerrillas and security forces during a seven-year-old separatist revolt against Indian rule in the Himalayan region.
Several times separatist and pro-government militants have forced newspapers to halt publication.
At least five journalists have been killed in the Kashmir Valley, and dozens have escaped attempts on their lives by unidentified gunmen.
Militiamen supporting Indian rule took 19 journalists hostage last July and threatened to kill four unless their editors agreed to meet them. The hostages were later freed by the army.
Dozens of guerrilla groups are fighting for independence or merger with neighbouring Pakistan, and at least three pro-India militia groups are helping paramilitary troops combat militancy.
